back.bio: I'm a Senior Software Engineer at Box. The work I keep coming back to is applied AI: find the annoying workflow, understand why it exists, and build something my teammates can actually use.

aiProfile.title: Applied AI, close to the work
aiProfile.tagline: I realized the trajectory for my career has fallen perfectly in place with the recent AI fad. I've spent a lot of time automating systems: at school, at home, at work...
aiProfile.summary: A lot of my recent work started with an annoying problem: forecast context spread across docs, sheets, Slack, and people's heads. I built tools around that. Nimbus made forecast Q&A less dependent on me. Cadence made recurring team work less scattered. OpenClaw and Hermes are where I'm testing what personal agents can actually do.

highlights.name: Nimbus
highlights.detail: I built Nimbus as a Q&A knowledge base for forecast context. My teammates can ask questions that used to depend on me remembering where the answer lived.

highlights.name: Cadence
highlights.detail: I used Cadence to pull recurring work into a more repeatable path: JIRA, Confluence, service-desk work, roadmap questions, and the small things that quietly pile up.

highlights.name: OpenClaw and Hermes
highlights.detail: OpenClaw and Hermes are where I'm pushing on agents more directly: memory, tools, context, and what it feels like when the agent is actually useful.

highlights.name: Signals
highlights.detail: I started turning forecast changes into persistent line items at our most atomic level. The old version left too much context in sheets and people's heads.

highlights.name: What I want more of
highlights.detail: I want to keep building scalable, reliable, resilient AI tools.

direction: The problem is still fuzzy, but everyone can feel the pain.
